title: The global search PR queried MailAccount and MailRule with plain .objects.filter() behind only a model-level has_perm check, unlike the owner-aware get_objects_for_user_owner_aware() it used for tags and correspondents, so users see other users' mail accounts and rules.

findings.explanation: All database queries use Django ORM with parameterized filtering (filter(), get(), icontains). The user-supplied 'query' parameter is passed only to ORM methods that properly escape and parameterize values. No raw SQL or string interpolation into queries is present in the diff.

The GlobalSearchView checks `request.user.has_perm('documents.view_document')` etc. before querying most objects. However, for users (User model) and groups (Group model) referenced in the test, there are no permission checks shown in this diff fragment (the diff cuts off). Additionally, the SearchResultSerializer was moved from views.py (where it had PassUserMixin) to serialisers.py without PassUserMixin, which may mean the serializer no longer has access to the request user for ownership-aware filtering. The Document.objects.get(id=instance['id']) in the new SearchResultSerializer location in serialisers.py does not perform any ownership/permission check — it fetches any document by ID from the search index result without verifying the requesting user owns or has access to it. This relies entirely on the search index being correctly scoped, but if the index returns documents the user shouldn't see, they'd be exposed.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore PassUserMixin on SearchResultSerializer or pass the request context through to the serializer. Also ensure that the Document.objects.get() call in SearchResultSerializer.to_representation() is scoped with an ownership-aware queryset (e.g., get_objects_for_user_owner_aware) rather than the global Document manager, to prevent information disclosure if the search index is not perfectly scoped to the requesting user's permissions.
